current_formulation: Article-to-headline stance is scored with class-wise and macro-averaged F1, which the majority class does not dominate.

steps.formulation: Stance is whether the author of a text is in favour of, against, or neutral towards a target.
steps.quote: Stance detection is the task of automatically determining from text whether the author of the text is in favor of, against, or neutral towards a proposition or target.

criticism.quote: systems found it markedly more difficult to infer stance towards the target of interest from tweets that express opinion towards another entity.

steps.formulation: FNC-1 labels a news article as agreeing with, disagreeing with, discussing, or unrelated to a headline. Known through Hanselowski et al.
steps.quote: The goal of the FNC-1 challenge is to determine the perspective (or stance) of a news article relative to a given headline.

criticism.quote: FNC-1's proposed evaluation metric favors the majority class

steps.formulation: Class-wise and macro-averaged F1 replace the FNC-1 score.
steps.quote: we propose the class-wise and the macro-averaged F1 scores (F1 m) as a new metric for this task
